decisions.question: Use the lookup AbortSignal for retry waits
decisions.chosen: Use the lookup AbortSignal for retry waits
decisions.reasoning: One shared signal enforces the total two-second diagnostic budget across fetches and backoff sleeps.

decisions.question: Use an exact-checkout public CLI proof with a fake local broker and Cloud 404
decisions.chosen: Use an exact-checkout public CLI proof with a fake local broker and Cloud 404
decisions.reasoning: This captures the operator-visible mismatch on base and the LOCAL-ONLY/SSH guidance on head without pretending the Cloud-only attach route is self-hostable.

decisions.question: Cap the optional Cloud name lookup at two seconds
decisions.chosen: Cap the optional Cloud name lookup at two seconds
decisions.reasoning: The macOS E2E showed the 10-second lookup budget could exceed node status's established 10-second command deadline after local broker readiness; two seconds keeps the diagnostic useful while preserving local status responsiveness.

decisions.question: Add the SSH fallback directly to node_not_found attach errors
decisions.chosen: Add the SSH fallback directly to node_not_found attach errors
decisions.reasoning: Option B requires both status visibility and an actionable --node failure; a conditional hint is accurate without claiming the caller's missing Cloud name definitely exists locally.

decisions.question: Reconcile node status against the Cloud name endpoint instead of treating websocket connectivity as registration
decisions.chosen: Reconcile node status against the Cloud name endpoint instead of treating websocket connectivity as registration
decisions.reasoning: Live inspection showed the second broker eventually appears in Cloud, so multiple brokers are supported; the failure window is local readiness advertising a name before the Cloud REST lookup used by --node can resolve it. Status now reports registered, confirmed LOCAL-ONLY, or unknown and gives SSH/state-dir guidance.
